pillars.engagement_stem: You are more likely to contribute your time, effort and identity into a group

NormExp.name: Normative Expression
NormExp.description: Similar to Group Think, this Pillar is your willingness to defend the status quo by expressing opinions in support of it, and suppressing other member's suggestions to change it (DivsExp). This would damage any norm of Psychological Safety, however it is entirely possible that you personally feel high DivsExp while wanting to maintain control of other people's DivsExp. In other words, that no one else's suggestions but your own should be listened to.

anchors.10: You wholeheartedly endorse the status quo and are completely unwilling to hear other member's suggestions to change it.
anchors.1: You are open to hearing other member's suggestions and listening intently when they do.

NormExp.effect_on_other_pillars: NormExp has a delayed impact because it is assumed that your suppression or welcoming of ideas has already occurred. As with DivsExp, there is no assumption that any opinion has been acted on (although the scenario may play out that way).
NormExp.engagement: Where you feel that you can manage (minimise unwelcome or surprising) change, by using your power to reduce any propensity for others to suggest change. While high NormExp undermines Psychological Safety for others, it makes you personally feel safer.

pre_language.core: Holding to the group's settled ways and keeping others to them: threatening, cutting off or turning away from anyone who starts something different, and feeling safer for it. Intimates read it from how she meets another's new way.
pre_language.10: She keeps to the usual ways and threatens, cuts off or turns her back on anyone who starts something different.
pre_language.1: When another starts something different, she turns to watch, waits to see where it goes and lets them try, sometimes following.

DirRecip.name: Direct Reciprocity
DirRecip.description: This Pillar reflects your willingness to participate in a norm where assistance is only rendered with expectation of repayment. It is provision of conditional assistance to others in the group, or acceptance of conditional offers from them. Costs that might be factored in to the decision include distraction from your current tasks (when helping another) or the risk of rejection when offering or supplying help. Evolutionary psychologists find that the norm of DirRecip is more common in primates, including Bonobos who will trade sex for other favours. Generally, a group's culture will be dominated by DirRecip or IndRecip, but not both.

anchors.10: You will provide to or seek assistance from any group member, when there is some indication that reciprocation can occur in future ('handshake deal').
anchors.6: You will only consider providing or seeking assistance when reciprocation is obviously possible ('money up front').
anchors.1: Even when reciprocation is possible, you will not consider assisting or being assisted ('no deal').

DirRecip.effect_on_other_pillars: DirRecip's impact on other Pillars is based upon the assumption that assistance has been received. As such, it moves forward in time to the help having been rendered, and the reciprocal debt incurred. The provision of assistance is not modelled because its impacts are less predictable. There is no Force card drawn if the character has provided assistance.
DirRecip.engagement: Where you feel that the norm of DirRecip is strong because the group can adapt to challenges smoothly by moving effort to where it is most urgently needed, by trusting each other's word (assuming there are favours that each can do for each other); there is joy in feeling part of an endeavour where promises to return favours are always kept, and your efforts end up being recognised and returned; this version of trust is more honouring a deal, rather than being trusted to carry out tasks reliably (as per IncResp and OutResp).

bars.anchor: Trades favours with anyone on a handshake, trusting any sign that the return can come later; keeps every promise and expects the same.
bars.within: 10 extends credit to anyone; 9 to those with some track record.

bars.anchor: Helps and accepts help when a return looks likely, keeping a loose mental ledger; gives credit to people who have repaid before.
bars.within: 8 carries open debts comfortably; 7 prefers them settled soon.

bars.anchor: Helps or accepts help only when the return is obvious and close ('money up front'); uneasy carrying open debts.
bars.within: 6 deals when the return is certain; 5 needs it immediate.

bars.anchor: Wary of deals; declines most offers and rarely asks, seeing a debt as more trouble than the help is worth.
bars.within: 4 will still trade with a trusted partner; 3 won't.

bars.anchor: Won't help or be helped even when a return is plainly on offer ('no deal').
bars.within: 2 might accept a settled, one-off exchange; 1 refuses.

pre_language.core: Give and take kept in balance: grooming for grooming, support for food, sharing with those who share. She watches who has given, gives to them and holds back from those who have not; intimates read it from steady trading partnerships.
pre_language.10: She grooms, shares and backs anyone who has given before or looks likely to, trusting the return to come later, and returns what she gets.
pre_language.1: Even with a partner who has given to her, she does not groom, share or back them, and turns away what is offered.

IncResp.name: Incoming Respect
IncResp.description: This Pillar is the extent to which others respect your competence and count on you to deliver your part of the group's work. In sum total, IncResp is other's assessment of your ability to deliver for the group. Noting however, it is your opinion of that assessment, which if people do not tell you explicitly, must be inferred.

anchors.10: You believe that others find you highly competent and reliable.
anchors.1: You believe that others find you highly incompetent and unreliable.

IncResp.effect_on_other_pillars: You respond to the current assessment of others' respect for you.
IncResp.engagement: Where you feel that others have a high opinion of your competence and trustworthiness: you feel valued and understood; you feel that others regard you to be a legitimate and useful member of the group; your identity as belonging to this group is consistent with others' appraisal of you.

pre_language.core: Feeling counted on for her part: others watch her work, copy her, bring her the task or leave it in her hands, and wait for her to finish it. Intimates read it from whether others rely on her or take over from her.
pre_language.10: Others watch her work, copy her, leave the task in her hands and wait on her; she sets to it with assurance.
pre_language.1: Others take the task from her, push past her to do it, or ignore her attempts; she hangs back.

OwnProsp.name: Own Prospects
OwnProsp.description: This Pillar is the likelihood of achieving your personal ambitions within the group. If joining a sports team, it might be a high number of scores for the season. Note it is not that the goals have been achieved, but rather the chance that they will be. Once achieved, the goals are no longer relevant to OwnProsp, except to the extent of being evidence that you can do so again (assuming your goals remain similar).

anchors.10: You believe it is almost certain that your personal goals will be achieved.
anchors.1: You believe it is almost certain that your personal goals will not be achieved.

OwnProsp.effect_on_other_pillars: You respond to your current assessment of goal achievement likelihood.
OwnProsp.engagement: Where you feel that you are likely to achieve your personal goals, whether or not they are part of the group goals (GrpProsp) or indeed, conflict with them. Presumably if personal and group goals are in conflict, you would prefer to have low levels of GrpProsp however such a condition is out of scope for the model as it indicates deception and potentially sabotage, which is a cognitive rather than an unconscious drive (as the Pillars are contended to be).
OwnProsp.out_of_scope: Personal goals deliberately in conflict with group goals (deception, sabotage).

pre_language.core: Hope, or hopelessness, about getting what she herself is after (food, a mate, a place, a skill) while living among the group. Intimates read it from how she pursues her own aims: with persistence and energy, or listlessly.
pre_language.10: She goes after what she wants with energy and keeps at it, expecting to get it.
pre_language.1: She gives up on her own aims early, listless, expecting to miss out.

Status.name: Status
Status.description: This Pillar is your felt place in the group's settled order of rank: how far others defer to you, give way to you and accept your decisions on behalf of the group. The rank may be conferred formally (an office, a title, a vote) or settled informally over time; what matters is that all recognise it and it need not be renegotiated each time. Deference here goes to your place, whatever others think of your skill.

anchors.10: Everyone in the group gives way to you, and no one acts against your decisions.
anchors.1: You give way to everyone, and your decisions carry no weight unless others approve them.

Status.effect_on_other_pillars: Your perception of your status can change due to slight changes to a formal remit, or the willingness people are to be compelled. If they do not respect your authority, you would feel lower status, and influence your behaviour.
Status.engagement: Where you feel that you possess formal power within a group, enabling you to utilise the group to achieve your own vision, which aligns the group with your identity. This is why new leaders often revoke measures taken by the preceding.

bars.anchor: Holds most of the formal power, and others act on their word without question.
bars.within: 10: nothing moves without them; 9: some matters sit elsewhere.

bars.anchor: Holds real authority over others in their area; it is accepted and rarely tested.
bars.within: 8: accepted by all; 7: occasionally queried.

bars.anchor: Holds a formal say in limited matters, but others don't reliably treat it as binding; they may bypass it or go over their head.
bars.within: 6: usually honoured; 5: often worked around.

bars.anchor: Little formal power; what they have is easily bypassed, and anything beyond routine needs approval.
bars.within: 4: a small say that holds; 3: one that rarely does.

bars.anchor: No formal power, or a nominal role no one heeds; must seek permission for any action.
bars.within: 2: a title without weight; 1: not even that.

pre_language.core: Her felt place in a settled order of rank that all recognise: others yield space and food to her, greet her with submissive signals and wait for her before moving, or she yields, greets and waits on them. Intimates read it from who gives way to whom.
pre_language.10: Others give way to her at food and resting places, greet her submissively and wait on her before acting; she can displace anyone.
pre_language.1: She gives way to everyone, greets others submissively, and waits for their tolerance before taking food or space.

Yet both may be the product of common consent, such as voting. The difference is the formalisation of the power, rather than being informal and thus needing to be negotiated.

DivsExp.name: Diverse Expression
DivsExp.description: This Pillar is what extent your ideas challenging Group Think will be listened to. Not necessarily heeded, although an idea may of course be enacted. Your contribution will involve (or imply) some change to the status quo, such as to authorities, roles, processes, and group goals. DivsExp is related to the norm of Psychological Safety more than to common understanding of freedom to act. Since it relates to a group, no member should be acting unilaterally, or at least outside of their agreed roles and responsibilities. Thus, DivsExp is freedom to suggest change to such constraints.

anchors.10: You have absolute confidence that your suggestion for change will be listened to and then considered by the group in a way that respects its complexities and nuances.
anchors.1: You believe that your suggestions will be ignored, or not given due consideration even if (grudgingly) heard.

DivsExp.effect_on_other_pillars: DivsExp has a delayed impact because it takes time for your contribution to either heard or ignored. Again, there is no assumption that it has been or will be acted on (although the scenario may play out that way).
DivsExp.engagement: Where you feel that your ideas will be welcomed and well-received. While related to IncResp (HCP), Expression is closer to a norm of Psychological Safety than being given specific respect for one's competence. Such a norm creates a warm, less hostile environment, which is distinct from cohesion: a close, friendly group can still make challenge feel risky.

was.description: This Pillar is what extent your ideas challenging Group Think will be listened to. Not necessarily heeded, although an idea may of course be enacted. Your contribution will involve (or imply) some change to the status quo, such as to authorities, roles, processes, and group goals. DivsExp is related to the norm of Psychological Safety more than to common understanding of freedom to act. Since it relates to a group, no member should be acting unilaterally, or at least outside of their agreed roles and responsibilities. Thus, DivsExp is freedom to suggest change to such constraints. Its reactive core, older than language, is latitude: feeling free to act differently from the group, or to start something new (a new way of doing a task, a new route), without being slapped down. Spoken suggestions are today's chief form of it.

anchors.10: You have absolute confidence that your suggestion for change will be listened to and then considered by the group in a way that respects its complexities and nuances. You feel free to try things differently, and do, without bracing for a slap-down.
anchors.1: You believe that your suggestions will be ignored, or not given due consideration even if (grudgingly) heard. You hold back from doing anything differently, expecting to be slapped down.

pre_language.core: Being attended to when you start something new: others turn to watch, wait to see where you go, and sometimes follow or copy; and being free to do so without being slapped down. Watching is the listening; following or copying is the heeding, which DivsExp does not require.
pre_language.10: When you start something different, heads turn, others wait to see where you go, and some follow or copy; you try new ways freely, without bracing for a slap-down.
pre_language.1: When you start something different, no one looks or follows, or someone above cuts you off; you hold back from doing anything differently.

GrpProsp.name: Group Prospects
GrpProsp.description: The extent to which you believe the group will achieve its planned goals (as opposed to your personal objectives, or fortunate gains). Once goals have been achieved, they are no longer a factor in GrpProsp. It is only concerned with future goals that remain to be achieved. This is because already-achieved goals may not continue to influence your engagement, because you have already experienced the benefit, and new goals may be substantially different. Like a hunting party having caught the antelope, and distributed the meat, however if there are no more antelope around, you may not think this group will be as successful hunting mammoth. Of course, ability to coordinate effectively is a generic group attribute, which would assist hunting ANY animal. GrpProsp is designed to capture overarching group efficiency, and the general problem space, but given specific, agreed, yet-to-be achieved goal/s.
GrpProsp.footnote: A group with goals is formally defined as a team, but the term group is preferred as it removes the implication of a wider organisation and hierarchy.

anchors.10: The group is almost definitely likely to succeed in its goals.
anchors.1: The group is almost definitely likely to fail in its goals.

GrpProsp.effect_on_other_pillars: GrpProsp's impact on other Pillars is based upon your present assessment of the average group attribute. In other words, the goal still remains to be achieved.
GrpProsp.engagement: That is likely to succeed in goals that you believe are worth pursing, or you would not have joined the group in the first place, and that has agreed goals, or otherwise random changes to the group's direction will move outside the model's ability to predict.
GrpProsp.out_of_scope: Random changes to the group's direction without agreed goals.

pre_language.core: A shared feeling that the band's joint venture (a hunt, a move, a defence) will come off, or will fail. Intimates read it from how members set about the venture together: in step and with energy, or straggling and flagging. It concerns the venture still ahead, not one already won.
pre_language.10: Members set off on the shared venture together, keep pace, stay close and press on; she throws herself into it eagerly.
pre_language.1: Members straggle, falter mid-venture or drift off; she slows, looks about, or stops trying.

IndRecip.name: Indirect Reciprocity
IndRecip.description: This Pillar reflects your willingness to participate in a norm where assistance is rendered without expectation of repayment. It is provision of unconditional assistance to others in the group, or acceptance of unconditional offers from them. In either case, costs that might be born include distraction from your current tasks (when helping another) or the risk of rejection when offering or supplying help. Evolutionary psychologists believe that the norm of IndRecip underlies and distinguishes human from primate collaboration. Generally a group's culture will be dominated by DirRecip or IndRecip, but not both.

anchors.10: When the need arises, you will provide to or seek assistance from any group member.
anchors.1: Even when there is a need, you will not provide nor seek assistance.

IndRecip.effect_on_other_pillars: IndRecip's impact on other Pillars is based upon the assumption that assistance has been received. As such, it moves forward in time to the help having been rendered. The provision of assistance is not modelled because its impacts are less predictable. There is no Force card drawn if the character has provided assistance.
IndRecip.engagement: Where you feel that the norm of IndRecip is strong because the group can adapt to challenges smoothly by moving effort to where it is most urgently needed, without needing to debate or cajole, and there is joy in feeling part of collective endeavour where no one prioritises self-interest or their own immediate tasking.

bars.anchor: Offers help to, or asks it of, anyone in the group as soon as a need appears, with no thought of return; effort flows to wherever it's needed.
bars.within: 10 includes people outside their usual circle; 9 hesitates there.

bars.anchor: Helps and accepts help freely without keeping score, though a heavy load or an unfamiliar colleague can make them hold back.
bars.within: 8 seldom holds back; 7 does when busy.

bars.anchor: Unconditional help happens some days and not others, depending on who and how busy; unsure whether others would pitch in for them.
bars.within: 6 leans towards helping; 5 waits to see.

bars.anchor: Rarely offers help unprompted and hesitates to ask for it; accepts help when it comes but doesn't count on it.
bars.within: 4 still accepts readily; 3 is surprised by it.

bars.anchor: Neither offers nor seeks help, even when the need is plain; assumes everyone is left to their own tasks.
bars.within: 2 might accept help pressed on them; 1 won't.

pre_language.core: Readiness to help and be helped without any tally: moving in to help someone who is struggling, sharing, consoling, and taking help offered, with no watch kept on returns. Intimates read it from easy, unasked help flowing both ways.
pre_language.10: When anyone struggles she moves in to help unasked, and when she struggles she takes help readily; no one watches for a return.
pre_language.1: She watches others struggle without moving to help, and turns away help offered to her.

OutResp.name: Outgoing Respect
OutResp.description: The extent to which you believe other group members are competent and trustworthy. Do they have the skills needed for their roles, and can they be relied upon to carry them out?

anchors.10: Others are extremely competent and absolutely trustworthy.
anchors.1: Others are completely incompetent and untrustworthy.

OutResp.effect_on_other_pillars: OutResp's impact on other Pillars is based upon your present assessment of the average group attribute.
OutResp.engagement: With competent and trustworthy people because you like being associated with 'winners', you admire and wish to model yourself off them, and they can help you to improve.

pre_language.core: Confidence in those around her: watching the skilful, copying them, following their lead and leaving tasks in their hands, without wariness that they will fail her or cheat her. Intimates read it from whom she watches, follows and relies on.
pre_language.10: She watches others' skill closely, copies them, follows their lead and leaves tasks to them without checking.
pre_language.1: She keeps her distance, ignores their attempts, watches them warily and does things herself.

Popularity.name: Popularity
Popularity.description: The extent to which you believe other group members like you. Do they have positive regard for and generally enjoy your company? Are they personally inclined towards giving you the benefit of the doubt and have no reason to cause impediments for you in the group? Being liked here means being welcome as one of us, someone who fits what the group is about, which is why the liked can sway it.

anchors.10: Group members (platonically) love you and will persistently seek your company.
anchors.1: Group members loathe and can't stand being in the same room as you.

Popularity.effect_on_other_pillars: Popularity's impact on other Pillars is based upon your present assessment of the average group attribute.
Popularity.engagement: Where you feel comfortable and accepted by the group members, who 'have your back' and will support you in the event of any difficulties, and where you enjoy the power of influence (informal leadership).

bars.anchor: Sought out and made welcome by nearly everyone; others would notice and mind if they were missing.
bars.within: 10 by everyone; 9 by all but one or two.

bars.anchor: Liked and included as a matter of course; given the benefit of the doubt.
bars.within: 8 by most; 7 by a solid core.

bars.anchor: Included when present, rarely sought; warm with some, neutral with others.
bars.within: 6 leans welcome; 5 is unsure.

bars.anchor: Overlooked: left out of talk and plans, not with hostility, and no one seems to notice.
bars.within: 4 still has one or two who reach out; 3 has none.

bars.anchor: Actively disliked or shunned; others avoid their company.
bars.within: 2 tolerated in the room; 1 not even that.

forces.explanation: Impending group failure or success has uncertain effects on reciprocal help. People might muck in together or lose heart. It largely depends on the quality of leadership

pre_language.explanation: When the shared venture looks to be failing, or succeeding, members may crowd in and work shoulder to shoulder, helping each other unasked, or lose heart and drift apart, each to her own; which way it goes depends on how whoever leads carries themselves.

reactive_test.reason: Heart lifted or lost is an emotional reaction; mucking in and drifting apart are pre-language acts. Leadership quality is a condition, not a calculation.
